 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Miami Heat are on the road Thursday night as they travel to take on the Golden State Warriors in an interconference matchup.
 Miami enters Thursday's game with a 3-5 record after defeating the Los Angeles Clippers on the road in overtime Wednesday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo (13) Sam Navarro-Imagn Images
 In Wednesday's victory, Bam Adebayo led the way for the Heat as he recorded 35 points, 10 rebounds and four assists while Klay Thompson added 30 points, five rebounds and three assists of his own.
 The Heat will try to grab another victory Thursday as they face off against the Warriors in a tough road matchup.
 Golden State enters Thursday's contest with a 5-3 record after defeating the Phoenix Suns at home Monday night.
 Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images
 Stephen Curry led the way for the Warriors in Monday's victory as he ended the game with 34 points, six rebounds and seven assists while Charles Bassey recorded 19 points and eight rebounds off the bench.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Thursday night's matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries.
 Heat Injury Report: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo Play?
 Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) Sam Navarro-Imagn Images
 The Heat have only one player listed on their injury report as they have listed Giannis Antetokounmpo as available as he will play despite dealing with a right wrist sprain.
 This is great news for the Heat as they will have their star forward in the second night of their back-to-back as they try to grab a key victory on the road over the Warriors.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Warriors Injury Report: Will Al Horford Play?
 Golden State Warriors center Al Horford (20).Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images
 The Warriors have four players listed on their injury report, though center Al Horford is not one of them.
 Of course, Horford missed Monday's victory due to back injury management but he is off the injury report and will return against the Heat.
 Golden State has ruled out Gui Santos due to left knee tendinitis as he will miss his second consecutive contest.
 The Warriors have also ruled out Kristaps Porzingis as he remains away from the team while Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody both remain sidelined while recovering from knee surgeries.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Fans can catch Thursday night's matchup between the Heat and Warriors from the Chase Center at 10 p.m. ET on NBA TV.
